postcards.title: Ginger on Cold Stone
postcards.caption: She found the one warm stone on the whole street and did not move for an hour.

postcards.title: The Second Rise
postcards.caption: The dough came up twice as fast on the warm ledge, and so did he.

postcards.title: School Shirt
postcards.caption: Dry by morning, from a beam nobody had thought worth looking for.

postcards.title: The Small Gear
postcards.caption: Sixty years of eyes, and the sun finally found the part that needed them.

postcards.title: Comic on the Stoop
postcards.caption: He read the last page in the light, then read it again to make it last.

postcards.title: Terrace Duet
postcards.caption: One tuned a string. The other slept through it, which was the correct answer.

postcards.title: Rooftop Coop
postcards.caption: Three birds, one ledge, no argument about who sat where.

postcards.title: Four Days of Night
postcards.caption: She had not seen the sun since Thursday. She saw it now, and shut her eyes on purpose.

postcards.title: Up from the Puddle
postcards.caption: The morning's rain came back as light for the tea.

postcards.title: Wet Paper
postcards.caption: The shade kept her colours honest. The cat kept the sun patch honest.

postcards.title: Chilies and Peas
postcards.caption: Half the lane dried red. The other half stayed cool enough to talk in.

postcards.title: Sorting Light
postcards.caption: Every envelope had a hand behind it. Out of the glare he could see them all again.

postcards.title: Banyan Shade
postcards.caption: Three neighbours, one bench, and a lamp that kept its counsel until the puddle spoke.

postcards.title: The Thimble
postcards.caption: A golden thread across a courtyard, to a thimble small enough to miss it.

postcards.title: Wind Chime
postcards.caption: The chime split the light the way it splits the wind: without asking.

postcards.title: Matched Squares
postcards.caption: Forty years of tea, and now the same patch of afternoon to drink it in.

postcards.title: Cellar Music
postcards.caption: He played by shade and listened by light.

postcards.title: Camelia at Dusk
postcards.caption: It opens only for rose-coloured light, which is a reasonable standard.

postcards.title: Pressed Flowers
postcards.caption: One beam, two quiet jobs, and no need to choose between them.

postcards.title: Three Windows
postcards.caption: The bells rang across the water, and the arch answered in lamplight.

postcards.title: Paper Boat
postcards.caption: It went as far as the rose-gold reached, which was far enough.

postcards.title: Last Tram
postcards.caption: The lantern held what the afternoon gave it, and gave it back at dusk.

postcards.title: Folded Warmth
postcards.caption: Two shifts of the sun to warm a chair she had been sitting in all evening.

postcards.title: First Star
postcards.caption: Shade for the telescope, light for the stairs, and the sky did the rest.

postcards.title: Fog Coming In
postcards.caption: Stored sun, carried up a staircase, spent on the way back down.

postcards.title: Glasshouse
postcards.caption: Rose-gold inside, indigo out, and not one leaf noticed the difference.

postcards.title: Supper
postcards.caption: Everyone from every shift, one long table, one last light.

postcards.title: Harbor Bell
postcards.caption: One beam, kept all evening, rung once.
